articleTitle: The impact of MPEG and DVB standards on broadcasting
publicationTitle: IEE Afternoon Seminar on Digital Television Broadcasting (Ref. No. 1998/419)
abstract: The broadcasting business has been undergoing significant change. Much of this change has been brought about by the advent of new technology which has been developing steadily in professional applications and has now become practical for consumer applications. The opportunities for direct transmission of new services in digital format which the new technology offers broadcasters and others are considerable and will radically re-shape and change the future of broadcasting. This paper briefly considers some aspects of this process and outlines those aspects of the new technology which are most important.

articleTitle: Image data compression-a time to take stock
publicationTitle: IEE Afternoon Seminar on Digital Television Broadcasting (Ref. No. 1998/419)
abstract: The technique of image coding (image 'compression'), resided in the research laboratory for several decades before the massive upsurge of interest in its application over the past ten years or so which now seems destined to leave the lives of few individuals in the developed world untouched. The development of the processing algorithms is discussed, together with the international determination to produce a set of standards. On the one hand, then, there were research workers around the world coding still images and video sequences at lower and lower rates, and on the other (once the discipline had matured sufficiently) increasing pressure to use the results gained in the laboratories as a practical way of overcoming the basic problem of the huge bandwidth or capacity needed to transmit or store an image of reasonable resolution in its uncoded form. The paper examines both of these activities, and their relationship, before seeing whether, indeed, there is now a logical way forward. The basic traditional techniques-prediction, transformation, motion compensation and variable wordlength coding form the basis of all activities presently proposed with the possible exception of MPEG-IV.

articleTitle: An overview of the development of digital terrestrial television in the UK
publicationTitle: IEE Afternoon Seminar on Digital Television Broadcasting (Ref. No. 1998/419)
abstract: The author begins with a brief history of digital television. The Digital Television Group (set up in 1995 and consisting of the BBC, BT, ITVA, C4, NTL, Pace, Motorola and Sony), its establishment and activities are discussed in particular. The digital TV receiver is also mentioned.

articleTitle: Some issues with ESGs and EPGs helping the consumer to navigate
publicationTitle: IEE Afternoon Seminar on Digital Television Broadcasting (Ref. No. 1998/419)
abstract: Within the context of a digital television broadcast, the essence of a guide is that it should provide information to a viewer that he may choose what to watch (listen or take part in). Further, that it should be possible for a viewer to make a selection based on the composition of a program or event offered within a service. Of course the receiver has to capture the details of whatever is capable of being received and thus it must also have some native awareness of the environment in which it is placed. An ESG (event schedule guide) takes, as its reference, the fact that to a very large extent, this information can be readily provided by the service information which can accompany any DVB broadcast. This SI is quite efficient at providing this core data both in terms of bit-rate and in terms of the amount of data required. Outline calculations indicate that around 30 kbit/s will support a 7 day schedule for a single multiplex in which each event can be described using the short event descriptor and yet the requirements for repetition rate set out in ETR 211 can be maintained.

publicationTitle: IEE Afternoon Seminar on Digital Television Broadcasting (Ref. No. 1998/419)
abstract: The Validate project started work in November 1995, when the DVB-T (digital terrestrial television transmission) specification was close to being finalised. It verified in detail the DVB-T specification and carried out technical work that will speed up the start of services. Validate is part of the ACTS programme sponsored by the European Commission as part of the fourth Framework programme. It is led by the BBC and includes several broadcasters and the EBU representing other public service broadcasters in Europe. Other participants include broadcasting research centres, telecom operators and both professional and domestic equipment manufacturers.
